newsitem.title: MEXICO: Analysts say Ahmsa Q2 disappointing.
newsitem.headline: Analysts say Ahmsa Q2 disappointing.

text.p: Mexican steel company Altos Hornos (AHMSA) turned in disappointing results on an operating level for the second quarter, analysts said.

The company reported second quarter earnings per share of 0.82 peso, a dive from a forecast 1.36 pesos per share in a Reuters survey of three analysts last week. In 1996, Ahmsa had earnings of 3.407 pesos per share for the period.
"At the operating level, excluding monetary factors, the results still look weak," New York Santander analyst Victoria Santaella told Reuters.
The lukewarm profits and growth levels reported on Wednesday could hold back expected earnings and operating margins for the year, analysts added.
Ahmsa said its net profits for the quarter fell 75.9 percent to 319.45 million pesos, from 1.323 billion pesos in the year-ago period.

The company attributed the fall mostly to three factors: a 12 percent drop in international steel prices, a severe hailstorm that halted operations at a furnace for nine days and a strong peso which hurt dollar-fixed sales.
"If the continue showing results like this quarter, they're going to be short on financing for their investment program," Santaella said.
Ahmsa is spending about $950 million in a five-year program to modernize its operations, lower energy costs and produce more value-added products.
Benefits that some expected from the projects by the second quarter should appear later in the year, analysts said.
"We expect the beginnings of the investment program should start to bear fruit and improve the operating margin later in the year," BBV-Probursa analyst Jose Buendia said.
Ahmsa's operating margin for the quarter was 16.3 percent, down from some analysts' forecast of at least 17 percent.
The company said the second quarter operating margin was hit by "unforeseen shutdowns of operational equipment and low steel prices."
But with a brand new coal-injection system and an oxygen and argon plant expected to come on line in the second half of the year, the company outlook appears more optimistic.
"Better operations margins should come later in the year," Valores Finamex analyst Chris Albi said.
Third quarter results should be favorable, he added, in contrast with a negative report for the quarter in 1996.
Albi said sales volume and production grew at a more sluggish rate in the second quarter than in previous quarters.
Steel product sales grew by 4.4 percent to 748,374 tonnes for the time period. Lower steel prices dragged down revenue 2.2 percent from the year-ago period to 2.900 billion pesos.
Production of liquid steel grew at a mere 0.5 percent for the quarter to 849,662 tonnes.
